text:
leah-rep: Heads-up team, Nimbus Health wants a short POC next week. They plan to host Redwood Private in their AWS account. Requirements: keep original client IP at the backend for logging & geo-blocking, preserve SNI so their TLS routing works with their ALB, and fast fallback to our hosted API if their TGW goes flaky. They also sent a security questionnaire and asked about expected EIP count and NAT impact. Can networking/security confirm recommended topology and what we need from them?

derek-net: Quick guide: best option for preserving client src IP is to use TGW/spoke routing or VPC peering with straight IP routing (no source NAT). If you front us with an NLB in IP mode or use TCP passthrough via an NLB pointing at ENIs, the source IP is preserved. PrivateLink (interface endpoint) will show traffic from the endpoint ENI to the service - so app sees endpoint IPs, not original clients.

derek-net: For SNI: if TLS is passed through (we don't terminate TLS), SNI is preserved. If they want TLS termination at our side (to inject headers like X-Forwarded-For), we need cert provisioning and to discuss key management with security.

olivia-se: Pricing note for the POC: we can cover up to 1 EIP per AZ for testing and one small NAT gateway for control-plane tasks. Production EIPs/NAT are customer costs. If they pick PrivateLink, ask them to allocate a /28 for our interface ENIs per region. Ill send the short pricing summary after this thread.

samir-sec: From security: we need the completed questionnaire (especially sections on key custody, VPC logging, and TLS termination). Required: KMS key ownership statement, VPC Flow Logs enabled (S3/CloudWatch destination + retention), and list of IAM roles we will assume (with least-privilege). Also confirm whether client-side TLS inspection exists in front of the connection.

tom-ops: Draft runbook / firewall snippet for their net team (drop-in):

Option A - TGW / peering (recommended for src IP):
- Routes: spoke subnet route -> TGW attachment for service subnets (no NAT).
- Security group on service subnets: allow inbound TCP 443 from spoke CIDR(s).
- NACL: allow ephemeral outbound >1024 for response if host-based rules used.
- Health/admin: allow TCP 15010-15012 from ops CIDR for health and debugging (time-limited).

Option B - PrivateLink (if customer requires endpoint model):
- Create Interface Endpoint(s) in their private subnets; ensure ENI IPs come from /28 reserved block.
- Security group on endpoint: inbound TCP 443 from spoke CIDR(s).
- Note: app will see endpoint ENI IPs as source; consider X-Forwarded-For if needed and if TLS termination allowed.

Example SG rule (copy):
```
Type: TCP
Protocol: 6
PortRange: 443
Source: 10.45.0.0/16  # example spoke CIDR
Description: allow app traffic from customer spoke
```

tom-ops: NAT note: If the spoke egress goes through a NAT gateway or egress proxy, source IP will be SNATed to NAT IP. To preserve client IPs you must avoid NAT on path.

deploy-bot: POC ticket created: RL-4627 assigned to @derek-net. Handoff checklist added: reserved /28 (if PrivateLink) OR route table screenshots + TGW attachment IDs. Delivery ETA: 48 business hours for connectivity doc.

julie-closer: Nimbus asked about RTO for failover to hosted API: they want <90s. Is that realistic?

derek-net: 90s is aggressive but achievable with active/standby + Route53 health checks + short TTLs. Two important caveats: some corporate proxies will take longer to fail open/close and TGW route propagation + endpoint health checks must be tuned. We'll include test playbook in the handoff.

leah-rep: Thanks. Action items: @olivia-se send pricing summary, @derek-net draft connectivity + test playbook, @samir-sec review questionnaire, @tom-ops finalize SG/NACL snippets and runbook. Customer uploaded questionnaire: https://s3.amazonaws.com/nimbus/poc/sec-q-2024.pdf. Schedule SRE sync Thurs 11am PT. :white_check_mark:
